en: The Great Compassion Heart Dharani of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Amoghavajra of the Great Tang.
I bow my head to Avalokiteśvara, Lord of Great Compassion, whose body of wondrous marks and signs possesses profound and vast vows of power;
adorned with a thousand arms, you universally protect and sustain, and with a thousand eyes of radiance, you observe all everywhere.
Within your words of truth you proclaim secret mantras, and from within your unconditioned mind, you give rise to compassion.
May all aspirations be swiftly fulfilled, And may all sinful karma be forever extinguished.
May the hosts of nāgas, devas, and noble sages protect you with compassion; May you suddenly cultivate and perfect hundreds of thousands of samādhis.
The body that upholds [this teaching] is a banner of radiant light; The mind that upholds it is a treasury of supernormal powers.

Washing away the dust of afflictions, I vow to cross the ocean; The gateway of skillful means for transcending and realizing Bodhi— I now recite this name and take refuge with a vow: May all my aspirations be fulfilled according to my heart.
Namo to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara! May I swiftly come to know all dharmas.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara; May I quickly attain the eye of wisdom.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara; May I swiftly deliver all sentient beings.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara; May I quickly attain skillful means.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara; May I swiftly board the ship of Prajñā.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara; May I soon cross over the sea of suffering.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara; May I swiftly attain the path of śīla and samādhi.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara; May I swiftly ascend the mountain of Nirvana.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara; May I quickly reach the abode of the unconditioned.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara; May I soon become one with the Dharma-nature body.
If I approach the mountain of blades, the mountain of blades shall crumble of itself;
If I approach the cauldrons of fire, the cauldrons of fire shall extinguish themselves;
If I approach the hells, the hells shall dry up of themselves.
If I face hungry ghosts, may the hungry ghosts be spontaneously satiated;
If I face asuras, may their evil minds be spontaneously subdued;
If I face animals, may they spontaneously attain great wisdom.
Having made this vow,
one should with a sincere heart invoke my name,
and should also single-mindedly recollect my original teacher, Amitābha Tathāgata.
Thereafter, one should immediately recite this dhāraṇī divine mantra.
By reciting it five times over the course of a single night,
the heavy sins of birth and death accumulated throughout hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas within one's body shall be eliminated.
Homage to the Tathāgata Amitābha; homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara. Again, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, if there are any among humans or devas..."
For those who recite and uphold these phrases of Great Compassion,
at the time of their death,
the Buddhas of the ten directions will all come to extend their hands to them.
"Whatever Buddha-land one desires to be born in,
one shall attain rebirth there according to one's vow.
He then addressed the Buddha again, saying:
World-Honored One, if any sentient beings who recite and uphold this Great Compassionate Divine Mantra should fall into the three evil realms,
I vow not to attain perfect enlightenment.
If those who recite and uphold this Great Compassionate Divine Mantra are not reborn in the lands of the Buddhas,
I vow not to attain perfect enlightenment.
If those who recite and uphold this Great Compassionate Divine Mantra do not attain immeasurable samādhi and eloquence,
I vow not to achieve perfect enlightenment.
For one who recites and upholds this Great Compassionate Heart Mantra,
if any of their aspirations in this present life are not fulfilled, [it shall be so].
It cannot be called the *Mahākaruṇā-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī*,
except for those who are unwholesome or lack sincerity.
If there are women who loathe and despise their female bodies, [they should recite it].
Those who wish to become men should recite and uphold the chapters and phrases of the Mahākaruṇā Dhāraṇī;
if they do not transform their female bodies into male bodies, [may I never attain enlightenment].
I vow not to attain perfect enlightenment.
Should anyone give rise to even a slight doubt, they shall certainly fail to achieve their goal.
If there are sentient beings who plunder or damage the food, drink, or property belonging to the Sangha, [they shall likewise fail].
Even if a thousand Buddhas were to appear in the world, they could not facilitate repentance for this;
even if one were able to repent, it would not be eradicated.
Now, by reciting the Great Compassion Mantra, it is immediately eradicated.
If one has encroached upon or damaged the food, drink, or property belonging to the Sangha,
it must be confessed and apologized for before the teachers of the ten directions;
only then will it be extinguished.
Now, when reciting the Mahākaruṇā Dhāraṇī,
the Buddhas of the ten directions immediately come to act as witnesses;
all karmic obstacles and hindrances are completely extinguished.
All those who commit the ten evil deeds and the five heinous crimes, who slander people and slander the Dharma,
who violate the precepts of communal discipline, break the precepts, destroy stupas, and ruin monasteries;
who steal the property of the Sangha and defile pure celibacy.
In this way, all such evil karmas and grave offenses shall be completely extinguished,
with one sole exception:
those who harbor doubts regarding the mantra.
Even minor offenses and light karmic actions cannot be extinguished,
let alone grave sins. Although these grave sins are not immediately extinguished, [they are nonetheless transformed].
It can still serve as a distant cause for awakening.
Again, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, if there are humans or devas who recite and uphold this Great Compassion Heart Mantra..."
One attains fifteen kinds of auspicious births and does not undergo fifteen kinds of inauspicious deaths.
As for those inauspicious deaths:
First, they shall not cause that person to die from hunger, starvation, or suffering;
second, they shall not cause them to die through imprisonment, shackles, or corporal punishment;
third, they shall not cause them to die at the hands of enemies or adversaries.
Fourth, they do not die by being killed in military arrays.
Fifth, they do not die by being mangled by tigers, wolves, or other predatory beasts.
Sixth, they do not die from being stung by venomous snakes, vipers, or scorpions.
Seventh, they shall not die by being burned or swept away by water;
eighth, they shall not die from being struck by poison;
ninth, they shall not die from being harmed by insects or venom.
Tenth, they do not die from insanity or loss of mindfulness;
eleventh, they do not die from falling from mountains, trees, cliffs, or precipices;
twelfth, they do not die from the malevolent sorcery of wicked people.
Thirteenth, one shall not die by falling prey to malevolent spirits or evil ghosts.
Fourteenth, one shall not die with a body ensnared by malignant diseases.
Fifteenth, one shall not die through self-harm in an improper manner.
Those who recite and uphold this Great Compassion Divine Mantra shall not suffer these fifteen kinds of evil deaths;
they shall instead attain fifteen kinds of virtuous births.
First, wherever they are born, they always encounter a virtuous king;
second, they are always born in a virtuous land;
third, they always meet with auspicious times.
Fourth, they constantly encounter virtuous friends.
Fifth, their physical faculties are always fully intact.
Sixth, their aspiration for the Way becomes pure and matured.
Seventh, they do not transgress the prohibitive precepts.
Eighth, all their kinsmen and retinues are harmonious and compliant in both affection and righteousness.
Ninth, their necessities, wealth, and food are always abundant and sufficient.
Tenth, one will always receive the respect and assistance of others.
Eleventh, all of one's wealth and treasures will not be plundered by others.
Twelfth, whatever one seeks according to one's intentions will all be fulfilled accordingly.
Thirteenth, they are constantly protected by nāgas, devas, and benevolent spirits.
Fourteenth, in whatever place they are born, they see the Buddha and hear the Dharma.
Fifteenth, regarding the true Dharma they hear, they realize its most profound meaning.
If there are those who recite and uphold the Mahākaruṇā Dhāraṇī,
they shall attain these fifteen kinds of virtuous births.
All devas and humans should constantly recite and uphold it, never giving rise to indolence.
After the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara had spoken these words,
he stood with palms joined before the assembled multitude and gave rise to a heart of great compassion for all sentient beings.
With a smiling countenance,
he then spoke these wondrous and sublime phrases of the Great and Perfect Unobstructed Compassionate Heart Dhāraṇī. The dhāraṇī says:
Namo haratana taraye. This is the original form of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
One should recite this with great compassion and focused attention;
do not raise the voice excessively, lest the divine nature become agitated.
First, *Namo ariye*: this is the essential body of the Bodhisattva Cintāmaṇicakra.
Upon reaching this, one must maintain focused mindfulness.
Second, *Varoṭe śvapre*: this is the essential body of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara holding the alms-bowl.
If you wish to collect the śarīra relics and bones, recite this while visualizing the Bodhisattva holding an alms-bowl:
*Oṃ sarvabodhisattvāya svāhā*. This is the Bodhisattva Amoghapāśa.
*Āḥ mahābala*. *Caturmahāsattvā vaye*. This is the seed-syllable of the Bodhisattva.
Reciting this mantra oneself is his very own essence.
Five: *Mahākāruṇika-ye*. This refers to the actual person of Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa;
he is the one holding the *ghaṇṭā* and *vajra* in his hands.
Six: *Oṃ*. This *oṃ* is for all the spirits and deities to join their palms and listen to the recitation of the mantra.
*Saptaparṇapāśye*: These are the actual names of the Four Great Heavenly Kings who subdue Māra.
*Sudhanadatta*: These are the names of the spirits belonging to the clans of the Four Great Heavenly Kings.
Ninth: *Namo siddhārtha īmo 're ya*. This is the original form of the Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna.
One must apply great effort in reciting this; do not let it slip away. The Bodhisattva is impatient.
10. *Po-lu-chi-ti-shih-fu-lo-han-t'o-po* (Parogitiśrīphaladhāpa): This is the Perfect Reward Body (*saṃbhogakāya*), Vairocana Buddha.
11. *Namo nara-gñi* (Namo naragñi): This is the Pure Dharma Body (*dharmakāya*), the original body of Vairocana Buddha.
One must apply great care.
*Dvādaśa hrīḥ mahāpātāśāme*. This is the "Bleating of Sheep," which refers to the deity Śirṣaka (the Goat-Headed King).
Together with all the devas and māras, they act as their retinue.
"Sarbathatadushpam" (薩婆阿他豆輸朋)—this is the nectar-like Bodhisattva;
he is also a member of the clan of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, serving as his retinue.
14. *Āśiveṅga*: This is the celestial king of the flying yakṣas, who patrols the four quarters to examine what is right and wrong.
15. *Sarvasattvanamopaga*: This is the divine king Vajradhara.
His form was black and massive;
he wore a loincloth made of leopard skin and held an iron blade in his hand.
The sixteenth is Maphasiddu; this is the original form of the Bodhisattva Cundī.
He holds an iron wheel and a noose, and possesses three eyes.
17. Tadyathā: This is the language of the sword.
18. Oṃ aparājitā: This is the essential body of the Great Brahmā Deva King. 19. Lokate.
The immortals constitute the tribal division.
Twenty: Kāratī; this refers to the deity Di, who is tall, black, and large.
Twenty-one: Ayuhri; this refers to the Heaven of the Thirty-three (Trāyastriṃśa).
This is the blue-colored Mahesvara Deva leading the celestial armies;
these twenty-two Mahābodhisattvas possess this true mind, free from any further confusion or distraction.
He is thus named Sattva.
Twenty-third, Sarvasarva—this is the Bodhisattva Gandhavyūha.
He commands the ghost-soldiers of the five directions as his retinue in an inconceivable manner.
Twenty-fourth: *māramāra*, this is the mark of a bodhisattva; the words of reprimand are thus completed.
Twenty-fifth: *mahe mahe lidaye*, as before.
The twenty-sixth is Kulukula-karma; this is the Bodhisattva Śūnyakāya, who leads two hundred trillion celestial troops as the Great General Who Subdues Heaven.
27. *Dulu, dulu, paśyate*. This is the Bodhisattva Saṃkramaṇa;
he subdues the barbarian armies of the Peacock King (*Mayūra-rāja*). 28. *Mahā-paśyate*, as before.
Twenty-nine: *Dhara dhara*. This is the Great Being, the body of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Thirty: *Dharini*. This is the Lion King.
Regarding the military omens for recitation:
in the thirty-first chamber is the Buddha Lavana; this is the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi (Pilik), who subdues all the retinues of Māras.
32. *Cchra cchra*. This is the essential body of the Bodhisattva Crusher, holding a golden wheel in his hand.
33. *Mama amuka dhāraya phamara*. This is the essential body of the Great Vajra Subduer of Māras.
34. *Kañcī*: This is the joining of palms by all Buddhas while listening to and reciting the mantra.
35. *Ihe ihe*: This is the Heavenly King Maheśvara.
Thirty-six: *na śi na*, the same as before.
Thirty-seven: *a ra kṣaṃ bha ra śari*. This refers to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
*Bha pi nu*: bow and arrow.
38. *Sa-pa-sa-pa* (the same as before). 39.
*Bhru-śaya*. This is the original body of Amitābha Buddha;
[he is] the presiding master of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Forty: *hulu hulu mara*. This refers to the eight classes of ghost-king deities (*bhūta-rāja*).
Forty-one: *hulu hulu he li*. [The meaning] is the same as before.
Forty-two: *sara sara*. This refers to the five turbidities of the evil world (*pañca-kāṣāya*).
Siri siri. This is Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
who brings inconceivable benefit to all sentient beings.
44. *Suru suru*: This refers to the falling of leaves from the trees of all Buddhas.
45. *Bodhiye bodhiye*: This refers to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
46. *Bodhaye bodhaya*: this is the original body of Ānanda. 47. *Maitrīye*: this is the Bodhisattva Mahāratna.
"Holding a golden knife in hand.
(48) *Nāraginchi*: This is the place where the Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna held a golden knife in his hand.
(49) *Dharisnina*: This is where the Bodhisattva Ratnaketu held an iron trident in his hand.
50. *Pāyamaṇa*: This is the bowl, vajra-pestle, and banner of the Bodhisattva Ratnakāñcanadhvaja.
51. *Svāhā* (in the departing tone).
52. *Siddhyaya*: This is the realization of all dharma-gates.
53. Svāhā (in the departing tone). 54. Mahāsiddhyai:
this refers to the Bodhisattva Emitting Light holding a crimson banner in his hand.
55. Svāhā (in the departing tone).
56. Siddhayoge: All these devas and bodhisattvas have gathered together;
they hold golden knives in their hands.
57. Śvāsa-rātra: This is安息香 (An-xi xiang, *śrīkhaṇḍa* or benzoin).
58. *Svāhā* (in the departing tone).
59. Nalajñe: the original body of the Bodhisattva Śailasāgara-mati, holding a golden sword in her hand.
60. Svāhā (with a departing tone).
61. Maṇiratna—this is the Jewel King Bodhisattva, who holds a golden axe in his hand.
62. Svāhā (with a departing tone).
63. *Sirasaṃ amukhaye*: This is the original form of the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja, who practices the healing of all diseases.
64. *Svāhā* (in the departing tone).
65. *Sava mahā-asitāye*. This is the original form of the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja;
he practices the healing of all diseases.
66. *Svāhā* (in the departing tone).
Sixty-seventh: *gilānāsītaye* (in unison). Sixty-eighth:
*svāhā* (in the departing tone). Sixty-ninth: *padumākeśitaye* (in unison).
70. *Svāhā*. 71. *Narakiñci-bagarāya*. 72. *Svāhā*. 73. *Mavari-śaṅkarāya*.

74. *Svāhā*. 75. *Namo hradatna-dharāya*. 76. *Namo araye*. 77. *Parugite*. 78. *Śavarāya*. 79. *Svāhā*. 80. *Siddham*. 81. *Mantāra*. 82. *Buddhaya*. 83. *Svāhā*. 84. (41) If one wishes for all sentient beings suffering from hunger and thirst, as well as all hungry ghosts (*preta*), to obtain cool relief.
Regarding the Amṛtahasta mantra:
Oṃ sru sru prasru prasru sru sru sruye svāhā. (7) If one is subject to fear and unease at all times and in all places, [one should recite this].
One should perform this at the hand that bestows fearlessness.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vajranātha hūṃ phaṭ (8). If one suffers from blindness or lacks the light of vision, [one should recite it].
One should recite the mantra at the Suryakānta-maṇi-hasta:
Oṃ dūbhika-ya dūbhi-pravāriṇe svāhā (9). If one suffers from a disease of hot poison and seeks coolness, [one should do so].
When [practicing] with the Candracāra-maṇi-hasta, the mantra is:
Oṃ susiddhikari svāhā (10). If one seeks to attain honor, promotion, or an official post, [one should recite this].
Regarding the mantra for the Archer of the Precious Bow:
Oṃ ājvāle svāhā (11). If one wishes to quickly meet with virtuous friends, [one should recite this].
When [practicing] with the Jewel-Arrow-Hand, the mantra is:
Oṃ kamala svāhā (24). If one wishes to be reborn in any of the Brahma heavens, [one should recite this].
When [the practitioner] holds the *kuṇḍikā* (water flask) in hand, the mantra is:
Oṃ vajraśekhara ruṭa maṭa. (12) If one is afflicted by various illnesses or difficulties of the body, [one should recite this].
When holding a willow branch in hand, recite the mantra:
Oṃ susiddhakaravāridānāṃ damuḍaye vajravajrapaṭahaṇa haṇa hūṃ phaṭ. (13) This is for the purpose of eliminating all evil obstacles and difficulties.
When holding a white whisk in hand, the mantra is:
Oṃ padmini pārvatī namo 'rjune namane svāhā. (14) If one wishes to bring about harmony among all kinsmen and followers, [one should recite this].
One should [recite] the mantra for the Jewel-Vase-Handed [Avalokiteśvara]:
Oṃ keli saṃpadye svāhā. (15) If one wishes to expel all tigers, wolves, and other malevolent beasts, [one should do so].
At that time, one should hold the side-tablet in hand and recite the mantra:
Oṃ bhaiṣajyanāthāya caṇḍadānuparīya bhaṣa bhaṣa svāhā (16). If one wishes to be free from the calamities of officials at all times and in all places, [one should do so].
When [reciting] the mantra for the one holding a battle-axe:
Oṃ vīraya vīraya svāhā (28). If one wishes to cause all spirits and deities to be non-resistant and compliant, [one should recite this].
For the mantra of the Skull-Jewel Staff-Holder:
Oṃ dhanavajra ṇi (29). If one wishes for the Buddhas of the ten directions to swiftly come and extend their hands [in blessing], [one should recite this].
One should hold a rosary in one’s hand and recite the mantra:
*Namo ratnatrayāya oṃ anavatīnījaye siddhisiddhārthe svāhā*. (4) If one wishes to subjugate all malevolent spirits and ghosts, [one should do so].
When [holding] a jeweled sword in the hand, the mantra is:
Oṃ teje teja-dṛṣṭi-vinirdeśa-devadhāya hūṃ phaṭ. (6) This is for the purpose of subduing all enemies.
One should [recite] the mantra at the hand holding the vajra:
Oṃ vajra-jñāna-pratipātaya svāhā (32). If one desires that benevolent deities and nāga kings constantly come to provide protection, [one should recite this].
The mantra for Kuśī-ayaḥ-aṅkuśa-hasta is:
Oṃ arhata-lakāra-viśaye namaḥ sarvaha (33). If one wishes to compassionately protect all sentient beings, [one should recite this].
The mantra for the hand holding the *khakkhara* (monk’s staff) is:
Oṃ nṛti nṛti nṛtya-pati nṛtya-nātha-paṇe hūṃ phaṭ. (18) If one desires various meritorious qualities, [one should recite this].
Regarding the mantra for the White Lotus-Hand:
Oṃ vajramālāya svāhā (19). If one wishes to seek rebirth in the pure lands of the ten directions, [one should recite this].
One should [recite] the mantra for the Blue Lotus-Handed One:
Oṃ kili kili vajrapūrapāṇa hūṃ phaṭ. (21) If one wishes to behold all the Buddhas of the ten directions face-to-face, [one should recite this].
One should recite the mantra for the Purple Lotus-Handed One:
Oṃ sarasara vajrakara hūṃ phaṭ (25). If one seeks to be born in the palaces of the various devas, [one should do so].
One should [recite] the mantra for the Red Lotus-Handed One:
Oṃ śaṅkari svāhā (20). If one wishes to accomplish vast wisdom, [one should do so].
When [practicing] with the Jewel Mirror Hand, the mantra is:
Oṃ visphuraṇāgra-khadira-maṇḍala hūṃ phaṭ (31). If one wishes to achieve eloquence and skillful speech, [one should perform this].
One should recite the mantra for the Jewel-Seal Hand:
Oṃ vajra-ñānadharaye svāhā (39). If one wishes for the Buddhas of the ten directions to swiftly come and bestow empowerment by touching the crown of one’s head, [one should do so].
When [the visualization] is at the hand of the emanated Buddha upon the crown of the head, the mantra is:

Oṃ vārye vāralambe svāhā (34). If one wishes to cause all ghosts, spirits, nāgas, snakes, tigers, wolves, lions, humans, and non-humans to always show respect, love, and mindfulness, [one should recite this].
When performing this with palms joined, the mantra is:
Oṃ visara visara hūṃ phaṭ (22). If one seeks various hidden treasures within the earth, [one should recite it].
The mantra for the Ratnapaṭṭahasta [deity] is:
Oṃ vajrapāśakaragrahaṇe hūṃ. (23) If one wishes to quickly accomplish the path of the Buddha, [one should recite this].
Regarding the mantra for the Five-Colored Cloud-Hand:
Oṃ vajra-karotāṃ ṭhaḥ (26). If one wishes to expel rebels, enemies, and adversaries from other regions, [one should recite this].
One should [recite] the mantra for the Jewel-Spear-Handed One:
Oṃ saṃmayā jina hāri hūṃ phaṭ (27). If one wishes to summon all the devas and benevolent deities, [one should recite this].
One should [recite] the mantra for Ratnaśaṅkhapāṇi:
Oṃ śaṅkari mahāsaṃpanne svāhā (1). If one desires various meritorious requisites for abundance, [one should recite this].
One should [recite] the mantra for the Cintāmaṇi-hasta:
Oṃ vajravatara hūṃ phaṭ (2). If one seeks peace and security from various forms of unrest, [one should recite this].
One should recite the mantra at the hand holding the noose:
Oṃ kīlara-mudrā hūṃ phaṭ (three times). This is for those suffering from various ailments within the abdomen.
When [performing this] for men, women,
or various servants and messengers, one should recite the mantra at the Hand Holding the Precious Bowl: Oṃ kili kili vajra hūṃ phaṭ (17).
When [holding] the jade ring in the hand, recite the mantra:
Oṃ padminīrāya svāhā (30). If one wishes to accomplish all sublime and wondrous Brahma-voices, [one should do so].
One should recite the mantra for the Jewel-Bell-Handed [Avalokiteśvara]:
*Namo bhagavatyai oṃ amṛte śrīye pūriṇe svāhā*. (5) If one wishes to subjugate all celestial Māras and followers of external paths, [one should do so].
One should recite the mantra for the Vajra-hasta:
Oṃ nīpe nīpe nīpaya mahāśrīye svāhā (35). If one wishes that, in every place of rebirth, one shall never be separated from the presence of the Buddhas, [one should perform this].
One should recite the mantra at the hand of the transformation Buddha:

Oṃ jvala raśmi ṭakki ṇikiri ṇikiri ṇi hūṃ phaṭ (36). If one wishes that, throughout all successive lives, one shall always abide within the palaces of the Buddhas and never receive a body born from a womb, [one should do so].
For the mantra of the Hand of the Emanated Palace:
Oṃ visara visara hūṃ phaṭ (37). If one desires to be intelligent, widely learned, and to never forget what has been studied.
One should recite the mantra at the Jewel Sūtra Hand:
Oṃ ahara sarvavinyadhāra pūṇite svāhā (38). If one wishes that from this present body until the attainment of the Buddha-body, the bodhicitta shall never regress; [one should perform this].
For one who possesses the non-retrogressive golden wheel in hand, the mantra is:
Oṃ śanamiśra svāhā (40). If it is for the sake of fruits, gourds, and various grains, [one should recite this].
Regarding the mantra for the Drākṣāhasta (Grape-hand):
Oṃ amala-khaṇḍe nini svāhā. After Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva had spoken this mantra, [he continued].
The great earth shook in six ways;
the heavens rained down a profusion of precious flowers;
and all the Buddhas of the ten directions were filled with joy.
The celestial Māras and followers of external paths were struck with terror such that their hair stood on end;
the entire assembly attained realization of the fruits,
some attaining the fruit of srotāpanna.
Some attain the fruit of once-returner (sakṛdāgāmin),
some attain the fruit of non-returner (anāgāmin),
